dossiers.title: API Architecture

requirements: Define API contracts independently from UI/provider internals.
Require explicit versioning, authentication/authorization context, idempotency and pagination/stream semantics.
Bind API errors to stable machine-readable failure/result contracts.
risks: UI-specific fields leak into core contracts

implementation_levels.name: Intent & ownership
implementation_notes: API Architecture owns only the behavior declared by its masterplan requirements; it must not become a shadow owner for adjacent planes.
Owned capabilities: versioned request/response APIs, operation lifecycle APIs, compatibility/error semantics.
acceptance: All production entrypoints resolve to one canonical owner for VOL-041.
Architecture validation rejects undeclared/shadow owners.

implementation_levels.name: Architecture & dependencies
implementation_notes: Canonical implementation surfaces: backend/routes, backend/core, machine/ai_runtime_schemas.json, backend/core/api_contract_registry.py, backend/core/routes_registry.py, backend/routes/operation_stream.py, machine/p1_api_contract_registry.json, scripts/check_p1_api_contract_registry.py.
Model/provider objects terminate at the adapter boundary; routing/inference decisions bind model, configuration, budget, privacy, and terminal reason.
acceptance: Dependencies are declared, acyclic at the governed layer, and compatible with machine/architecture.json.
A missing dependency or illegal edge fails before expensive/model work.

implementation_levels.name: Contracts & compatibility
implementation_notes: Primary contracts: ApiRequest, ApiResponse, ApiError, ApiCompatibilityPolicy.
Serialized/security-sensitive inputs use stable identity, version rules, canonical parsing, explicit absent/null semantics, and migration policy.
acceptance: Contract round trips and unknown/duplicate/malformed values are covered by negative tests.
Compatibility policy defines forward/backward behavior and rejects unsafe ambiguity.

implementation_levels.name: Admission & authority
implementation_notes: Define API contracts independently from UI/provider internals.
Principal/tenant, policy version, capability, budget, deadline and idempotency identity are attached before protected execution.
acceptance: Unauthorized or over-budget work consumes no privileged side effect.
Fallback never weakens privacy, residency, authority, or tenant isolation.

implementation_levels.name: Runtime control flow
implementation_notes: Require explicit versioning, authentication/authorization context, idempotency and pagination/stream semantics.
Canonical sequence: normalize -> authorize -> reserve -> execute bounded capability -> persist/emit -> verify -> finalize receipt.
acceptance: Cancellation/deadline propagates through every child operation.
No retry, recursion, delegation, search or background loop is unbounded.

implementation_levels.name: State & data semantics
implementation_notes: Classify all API Architecture data as authoritative, derived, cache, or ephemeral and assign one owner.
Durable writes require transaction/outbox or explicit idempotency/compensation semantics; derived state is rebuildable where declared.
acceptance: Acknowledged authoritative writes are not silently lost.
Retention/deletion/migration/rebuild semantics are executable for every persistent class used by the volume.

implementation_levels.name: Security, privacy & tenancy
implementation_notes: Treat external/model/tool/retrieval/file inputs as untrusted until validated at the owning boundary.
Threat/failure focus: version drift | ambiguous retry duplicates mutation | UI-specific fields leak into core contracts.
acceptance: Critical authz, tenant, secret, injection and data-boundary failures are non-compensable.
Logs/prompts/artifacts/telemetry contain no undeclared secret or protected data.

implementation_levels.name: Failure, resilience & recovery
implementation_notes: Open obligations: materialize API schema registry | bind compatibility tests to release gate.
Define timeout outcome semantics, retry budget, circuit/bulkhead/backpressure behavior, crash boundary, replay behavior, and recovery checkpoint for API Architecture.
acceptance: Fault injection covers dependency down/slow, crash-before/after-commit, replay, saturation, cancellation, stale evidence/worker, and rollback.
Recovery cannot create duplicate privileged effects or violate authority.

implementation_levels.name: Observability & operability
implementation_notes: Trace API Architecture from operation identity through decisions, dependencies, state changes, evidence and terminal result.
Emit structured metrics for success/failure, p50/p95/p99 latency where applicable, queue/resource pressure, retries, cost and recovery without hidden reasoning content.
acceptance: An operator can reconstruct a failed production operation without process-local memory.
Telemetry has bounded overhead and tested redaction.

implementation_levels.name: Performance, capacity & economics
implementation_notes: Comparator: thin REST wrapper around AI provider/runtime calls
Admission reserves scarce resources/cost before expensive work; saturation uses bounded queueing, routing, shedding, or rejection rather than uncontrolled degradation.
acceptance: Performance qualification includes tails and saturation, not median-only wins.
Optimization dequalifies automatically when source/policy/profile identity becomes stale.

implementation_levels.name: Verification & adversarial evaluation
implementation_notes: Focused test surfaces: backend/tests/test_api_contract_registry.py, tests/test_p1_api_contract_registry.py.
Evaluation surfaces: .github/workflows/p1-api-contract-registry.yml.

Verification must map each masterplan requirement, declared risk, trust boundary, concurrency invariant, and recovery obligation to deterministic tests or immutable evaluation evidence; every discovered failure becomes a versioned regression before promotion.
acceptance: Happy path, negative, adversarial, concurrency and recovery behavior are all exercised.
High-impact verification is independent or deterministically separated from the generator/implementation under test.

implementation_levels.name: Deployment, migration & rollback
implementation_notes: Deployment binds exact source, configuration, contracts, data migration, dependencies and artifact provenance.
Canary/readiness gates observe correctness, SLO, safety, cost and compatibility before promotion; rollback/reference fallback is rehearsed.
acceptance: No irreversible production change lands without explicit migration/reconciliation semantics.

implementation_notes: API Architecture exposes health/readiness distinct from semantic correctness, plus bounded diagnostic/support evidence.
Operator actions use preflight -> explicit admission -> execution -> immutable receipt; break-glass paths are scoped, expiring and auditable.
acceptance: On-call can identify owner, current state, dependency health, budget pressure, recent changes and recovery action.
Administrative actions cannot silently bypass policy or evidence requirements.

implementation_levels.name: Enterprise superiority & exit
implementation_notes: Primary superiority outcome: versioned, tenant-safe, normalized AI service boundary with idempotency and operation semantics

acceptance: Enterprise grade target is superior; current grade is designed.

Bind workload/dataset, model/provider where applicable, environment/hardware, policy/contracts, scorer, cost/resource budget, raw-result digest, and verifier verdict.
